BatteryCyclePenaltyPerKwh.title: BatteryCyclePenaltyPerKwh
BatteryCyclePenaltyPerKwh.description:
Penalty on battery throughput, incurred on both charge and discharge.

The default (~0.001) is a sensible choice for most cases — small enough that the
battery is used freely rather than left idle. Raise it under retail_rate_dispatch
to model real battery wear and prevent low-return arbitrage (cycles whose bill
savings don't justify the wear): there it is a degradation cost in $/kWh of
throughput, counted on both legs, so ~2x per delivered kWh (~$0.05–0.17/kWh: a
typical home lithium iron phosphate battery at the low end, a Tesla Powerwall
warranty at the high end). Under self_consumption it is not a dollar amount and
barely affects dispatch (the battery stores surplus PV whenever it can).
peak_shaving ignores it entirely: shaving a per-kW peak is not a per-kWh trade,
so it uses only a tiny internal floor.

from_datetime.title: From Datetime
from_datetime.description: Start of the requested interval range (inclusive). Interpreted as local wall-clock time at the building's location. CalibrationMethod.title: CalibrationMethod
CalibrationMethod.description:
Method for calibrating energy consumption. After the building ensemble is selected and
the initial loads are estimated, the calibration process will scale the estimated loads to better match
any known actual consumption data.
- 'uniform-mean' calculates an average multiplier for all actual consumption data points and then
  applies that multiplier to all timesteps uniformly.
- 'linear-interpolation' calculates multipliers for each time period and then
  linearly interpolates the multipliers for all other timesteps. For values outside the range of
  actual consumption data, the nearest multiplier is used. This method is intended to deal with buildings
  that may have varied over time (e.g., due to changes in upgrades, occupancy, or behavior).
- 'cyclic-regression' fits a regression model to the actual vs. estimated consumption data, and then
  applies that model to all timesteps. This method is intended to better capture cyclical patterns
  such as seasonal variations.

* energy (imports, exports, consumption, pv_production): the window over which

* demand: the window over which peak demand is measured and tiered bands applied.
* minimum: the period over which the minimum bill is evaluated.
* surcharge/tax: not applicable.

    * ClipBy='inner' (default): response will only include the full month of May.

DispatchStrategy.title: DispatchStrategy
DispatchStrategy.description:
Dispatch Strategy for battery.
- `RETAIL_RATE_DISPATCH` — minimize net electricity cost (pure arbitrage).
- `SELF_CONSUMPTION` — minimize grid import: store surplus PV and discharge
  it to cover later load, so as much load as possible is served on-site.
  Price-agnostic; the battery charges only from PV surplus (no grid-sourced
  charging), and surplus that won't fit still exports.
- `PEAK_SHAVING` — minimize the peak kW drawn from the grid (per billing
  period). Price-free: the battery charges, from PV or grid, to shave each
  period's peak draw rather than to arbitrage.

EnsembleAggregationMethod.title: EnsembleAggregationMethod
EnsembleAggregationMethod.description:
Method for aggregating a building ensemble.
- 'nearest' elects a single building from the ensemble. When actuals are provided,
  it selects the building with the lowest calibration error (MSE) relative to those actuals.
  When actuals are not provided, it selects the building closest to the median total
  energy consumption (electricity + fossil fuel) across the ensemble, using MSE as the
  distance metric.
- 'average' calculates a weighted average of all buildings in the ensemble. When actuals are
  provided, buildings are weighted based on calibration error (lower error = higher weight).
  When no actuals are provided, this is a simple unweighted average. Note that when using this
  method, ``floor_area`` is averaged across buildings even when their values differ, whereas
  other building attributes are only returned when they are common (equal) across all buildings
  in the ensemble. Future releases may provide distributional information for varying attributes.

RateType.title: RateType
RateType.description:
Identifies the type of bill line item a rate produces.

Each category determines what quantity (if any) the rate's amount
is applied to and where it fits in the bill calculation:

fixed: flat dollar amount per billing period
imports: $/kWh applied to electricity drawn from the grid
exports: $/kWh applied to electricity sent to the grid
net: $/kWh applied to net consumption (imports - exports); charges on positive net, credits on negative
net_imports: $/kWh applied to max(imports - exports, 0)
net_exports: $/kWh applied to max(exports - imports, 0)
demand: $/kW applied to peak power draw during the billing period
surcharge: percentage applied to net positive energy costs (e.g. 0.10 = 10%)
minimum: minimum dollar floor on the pre-tax subtotal
tax: percentage applied to the final subtotal (e.g. 0.07 = 7%)
pv_capacity: $/kW applied to installed solar system size
pv_production: $/kWh applied to on-site solar generation (e.g. PPA)
consumption: $/kWh applied to total home electricity consumption regardless of source (e.g. buy all sell all)

VariableModel.title: VariableModel
VariableModel.description:
Variables available for interval data.

Note: `costs.electricity.*` component variables are experimental and subject to change.

`costs.electricity.minimum_adjustments` is the per-period top-up applied to satisfy
a tariff's minimum-bill floor. Non-bypassable charges (fixed customer fees, demand
charges, and PV-capacity charges) count toward satisfying the minimum: the
adjustment is the gap between the minimum and the larger of (a) the period's
actual bill or (b) the period's non-bypassable charges. Net-export credits below
the non-bypassable floor are preserved in the imports/exports components rather
than being absorbed by the adjustment, so excess credits roll forward.
